text: Chíquiza (Spanish pronunciation: [tʃiˈkisa]) is a town and municipality located in the Central Boyacá Province, within the Colombian Department of Boyacá. It was previously known as San Pedro de Iguaque until July 17, 2003, when the name was officially changed to Chíquiza. The municipality lies on the Altiplano Cundiboyacense, with its urban center at an altitude of 2,900 metres (9,500 ft), and is situated 24 kilometres (15 mi) from the department capital, Tunja. It shares borders with Arcabuco to the north, Sora and Sáchica to the south, Villa de Leyva to the west, and Motavita to the east. The name Chíquiza originates from the Chibcha language, meaning "only" or "alone," with "Chiqui" interpreted as "priest"; an alternative origin is the word "chequiza," meaning "hairy field." Prior to the Spanish conquest, Chíquiza was part of the Muisca Confederation and governed by a cacique who remained loyal to the zaque of Hunza. The area held religious significance for the Muisca as it was near the sacred Lake Iguaque, considered the birthplace of Bachué, the mother goddess of the Muisca. Modern Chíquiza was founded in 1556 and was incorporated into Tunja until 1982. The local economy is based on agriculture and livestock farming, with primary agricultural products including maize, potatoes, peas, wheat, nabo, ibia, ruba, and onions. Its geographic coordinates are 5°36′N 73°29′W (5.600°N 73.483°W).
